handback.t:
R4-A3 / h3 DONE: calibrated confidence-gated verification. Every number is synthetic-until-validated-on-real-traffic. The confidence signals are synthetic (AUROC about .85 is my parameter, not a measured LLM property).

Files (all mine, no src edits, no commits, no downloads):
- C:\Users\mariu\neural-mesh\src\bin\h3_gate.rs
- C:\Users\mariu\neural-mesh\src\bin\h3_common\mod.rs
- C:\Users\mariu\neural-mesh\results\h3_gate_board_entry.md (VERIFY REQUEST blocks H3-A to H3-D with rerun commands, numbers, negatives)
- C:\Users\mariu\neural-mesh\results\h3_gate_all.{json,log}
- C:\Users\mariu\neural-mesh\results\h3_gate_confirm61-90_all.{json,log}
- C:\Users\mariu\neural-mesh\results\h3_proposed_patch.md (opt-in FixedGate proposal, not applied)

Rerun: `cargo run --release --offline --bin h3_gate -- --part all [--held 61-90]`, about 6.5 min each on 2 threads. `cargo test --release --offline --bin h3_gate` passes 4 tests, including exact reproduction of g9's agree/never/auto arms and g18's L2/L3 levels.
Build note: another worker's mid-edit src/memory.rs, compact.rs and tiered.rs broke the lib for a few minutes at a time during my session. My results come from a build taken when it compiled.

Design:
- Gate: verify iff signal <= t. t is fitted once on calibration seeds 101-130, which are disjoint from tune/held/confirm and asserted in code, then frozen. Nothing adapts online.
- Rules declared before running: R1 = cost-neutral break-even (headline); R2 = 0.90 error capture.
- Two independent generators:
  - G = W10's g9 critic world with the evidence verifier (12 worlds).
  - H = W19's g18 orchestration world with per-step verification (12 worlds).
- Signals: self-reported confidence, retrieval coverage/margin, and the orchestrator's router-posterior table (H).
- Baselines: never, always, W10 online `auto` (G), g18 L4 learned stopping (H), random-skip at equal total cost, oracle gate.
- Statistics: 30 paired seeds, 95% t-CI, Holm per family, equivalence margin +-0.01 declared in advance.
- Cost: every verifier execution is counted. G is reported at verifier price tp = 0.1 and tp = 1 call, both kept, neither chosen post hoc. H uses g18's own cost and utility.

Headline results (held 31-60 | confirm 61-90, c = 0.05; world G, AUROC .85, tp = 0.1):

| World | Verifier runs vs always | Accuracy vs always | Net vs always |
|---|---|---|---|
| A1 mixed | -30% / -32% | -0.0000 [-.0009,+.0008] / +.0004 (equivalent) | +.0027 / +.0032 |
| A9 rare errors | -69% / -67% | -.0018 / -.0016 | +.0036 / +.0037 |
| A7 weak retrieval | -73% / -77% | +.0172 / +.0152 | +.0302 / +.0286 |
| B1 4-claim reports | -51% / -48% | -.0037 / -.0030 | +.0057 / +.0058 |

- Targets met in G: A1 holds accuracy at about 30% fewer verifier executions and about 21% lower total cost. At equal cost the gate beats random-skip by about +1.5 points of accuracy (A1 +.0146 / +.0150). G-F4 (accuracy vs equal-cost random): 28 Holm wins and 2 losses of 48 tests, in both seed sets.
- Net gain over always is small at tp = 0.1, because a verifier run is cheap. The saving is in call count.
- W10's `auto` is almost identical to always-verify in 10 of 12 worlds, so gate wins over always are wins over `auto` (G-F6: 34 wins/4 losses at tp 0.1, 44/1 at tp 1).
- tp = 1: R1 cuts verifier runs by 63-97% (net vs always +.025 to +.074), but costs accuracy where errors are common (A1 -.0098, B1 -.0288).
- R2 is the same-accuracy rule: A1 runs -45% at accuracy -.0027 (equivalent), net +.0244 / +.0261.
- Calibration quality of the signal, held seeds: AUROC .85 (sep 1.5), .68 (weak), .49 (uninformative). Raw ECE is .07-.20, which becomes .002-.018 after binned recalibration fitted on the calibration split. The retrieval-coverage signal has AUROC .50 and only saves 2-4% of calls.
- Oracle gate: it verifies about 10% of tasks in A1 and is more accurate than the gate (+.009 accuracy over always, about 54% cheaper at tp 0.1).

Controls:
- Zero-error worlds (G A10/B3, H zero-err): R1 learns "never verify" and ties never exactly (net diff +0.0000 [0,0], 0 verifier calls).
  - Always-verify loses there: G -.0075/-.0138 at tp 0.1; H util -.011.
  - W10 `auto` loses -.0066 (Holm LOSS).
  - g18 L4 also loses in the H rare-error control (-.003/-.004) and confirm zero-error (-.0016, Holm LOSS).
- Uninformative signal (G NEG-A1/NEG-A9, H NEG-pipe/lat): R1 degenerates to the best fixed policy and ties it (exactly 0.0000 in NEG-A1), and ties equal-cost random in H. It ties because calibration finds the signal worthless, not because the signal helps. One confirm cell (NEG-A9 tp 1) is a Holm "LOSS" of 4e-5, still inside the equivalence margin.
- Failure shown: R2 does NOT tie on uninformative signals.
  - NEG-A1 at tp 0.1: net -.0060/-.0064 vs always, Holm LOSS.
  - NEG-A9 at tp 1: R2 collapses to always-verify and loses -.0434 vs never.
  - R2 ignores cost, so it needs an AUROC guard.

World H (second generator): this is mostly negative against the existing online rule.
- Calibrated gates match always-verify quality at about 91% fewer verifier calls. gate-post (router posterior), pipe-main: q .7694 vs .7696 at 0.48 vs 5.19 calls/task.
- They do not beat g18's online L4.
  - Utility vs best fair baseline: 4 wins/16 losses of 48 | 5/14.
  - Utility vs L4: 9/15 | 12/14.
  - Verifier-call reduction vs L4: 23/21 | 21/20.
- gate-post is within +-.01 of L4 in 10 of 12 worlds. It wins only where L4's online stopping is wrong: pipe-pricever, +.0207 | +.0220.
- The conf-only gate is q-lossy, about -.009 q vs always in pipe-main.
- Do not read H as "calibration beats online".

Where gating loses (shift tests; threshold from world X applied to world Y):
- Calibrated where verifying doesn't pay, tested where errors are common:
  - G A9 to A1, tp 1: accuracy -4.2 points (net still +.0152 vs always).
  - H rare-pricever to pipe-main: util -.0152 vs the in-distribution gate and -.0104 vs always.
- Calibrated on A1, tested on zero errors: over-verifies 65% of tasks, net -.0049 (tp 0.1) / -.0157 (tp 1) vs never.
- Weak signal (AUROC .68): at tp 0.1 R1 degenerates to always-verify with no saving. At tp 1 it saves 48% of cost but loses 1.9 points of accuracy.
- Expensive verifier with common errors (B1, tp 1): R1 stops verifying altogether (ties never), giving up 2.9 points of accuracy.
- A higher error rate at test (A1 to eps .4) was benign in G (+.0003).
- Thresholds moved between .35 and +inf across worlds, so calibration is needed per regime.

Disclosures:
- The test families vs auto/L4 and the cost-sign convention (always-minus-gate) were added after the first H run. Final files come from the final code with identical means.
- World lists, R1/R2, the margin and the tp/c grids were fixed in the source before running.
- Several worlds per generator are single-parameter variants of one base, so independence is across the G/H generators.
- The router-posterior signal is the orchestrator's own table, because the Router trait exposes no posterior.

Recommendation: nothing by default. If wanted, an opt-in FixedGate fitted offline per regime, with an AUROC >= 0.6 guard and a monitoring fallback to always-verify. In orchestration prefer g18's L4.
